initial:
Create a polished clinical comparison board for AVA's cosmetic-procedure visualizer. This is a new bitmap visual proof, not a photograph of a patient and not a surgical prediction. The attached image is a rough mannequin reference only: use the first figure's general adult proportions, disregard all other poses and text. Replace the rough render with exceptionally clean, professionally modeled, anatomically plausible 3D product-render quality.

Layout: exactly four columns and two rows, eight torso views total. Top row: identical straight front view. Bottom row: identical right-facing side profile. Column labels, once across the top, exactly: "Base", "Aumento", "Levantamiento", "Reducción". Small row labels: "Frente" and "Perfil". No other copy, no logo, no badges, no arrows, no claims.

Every figure is an adult female-shaped NONHUMAN display mannequin wearing the SAME fully opaque, seamless fitted warm-stone bodysuit, plain modest scoop neckline, broad shoulder coverage and mid-thigh legs. Covered breast and groin areas; no nipples or genital detail. Neutral medical/educational presentation. The garment must fit smoothly and continuously around rounded body forms, with understated believable seams, not armor, not rigid slabs, no block-shaped clothes, no cleavage opening. No skin photo effect, no sexualized pose. Sophisticated satin-matte ceramic-like figure with subtle surface detail and soft studio shading.

Crop all eight views identically from the base of the neck to the middle of the thighs, so the chest, waist and hips are large and easy to compare. Same shoulder height and pelvis height within each row; same camera distance, scale and framing. Arms relaxed slightly away from the torso, hands natural and unobtrusive; in the profile view keep the arm from obscuring the chest contour. All anatomy except the chest stays strictly identical between columns: abdomen, waist, hips, shoulders, arms, garment neckline, garment hems and posture. Do not rotate, arch or change the stance between variants.

Four deliberately DISTINCT yet plausible chest silhouettes under the opaque garment:
1 Base: moderately full breast mound with a slightly lower position and a softly descending lower pole.
2 Aumento: clearly greater volume and forward projection, fuller upper pole; the change must be immediately apparent, particularly in profile.
3 Levantamiento: approximately the SAME volume as Base, but the breast mound is visibly elevated with a shorter lower pole. Do not simply enlarge it. Do not move the neckline or the whole garment upward.
4 Reducción: clearly less breast volume, width and forward projection than Base, with a smooth natural convex chest. No dents, hollow cup impressions, rings, flat punched-in surfaces, sharp ridges or craters.

Prioritize believable anatomical contours and differentiation above decorative effects. Inspect the eight figures as if art-directing a premium anatomy visualization: flawless continuous shoulders, arms and torso, smooth convex breast contours, no damaged joints or floating anatomy. Warm ivory backdrop (#f5f1ea), espresso lettering (#241b16), generous quiet spacing and restrained modern humanist sans-serif typography. Consistent soft key light from upper left, broad gentle fill, fine ambient shadow, balanced exposure with visible midtones and no blown highlights. Refined AVA editorial presentation. Wide landscape board, high resolution, sharp full-quality rendering.
targetedRevision:
Edit this comparison board with one narrowly targeted anatomical correction. Preserve the board layout, every label, typography, ivory background, lighting, material, neckline, hems, crop and all body parts outside the chest. Preserve the Base, Aumento and Reducción columns completely unchanged.

Only correct the two figures in the THIRD column, labelled "Levantamiento". The front and side views currently look somewhat smaller in breast volume than Base. Make this column demonstrate ELEVATION while retaining approximately the original Base breast volume: lift the lower pole upward, redistribute the fullness into the upper breast mound, preserve a gently convex natural contour with comparable total fullness to Base, and keep a clearly higher mound position. It must differ from the smaller Reducción column AND from the enlarged, more projecting Aumento column. The side profile is critical: a raised breast mound of Base-like size, not a smaller mound. Do not just raise the entire garment or alter its neckline. The mannequin's shoulders, ribcage, waist, abdomen, hips, arms, hands, pose and scale remain exactly unchanged. Preserve the fully opaque modest bodysuit and nonhuman medical mannequin presentation. No exposed breast or groin anatomy. No new text or annotations. This is an educational comparative design study, not a clinical result prediction.
